title: 1.1 · Every riser in the flight
bodyHtml:
1.1 · Every riser in the flight

Target: tr.u2.stair-why; drawing: tr.u2.stair-sect

Materials

Rule, level, low stair model or approved observation route.

Fallback

Use provided readings on paper; mark field measurement not observed.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. There is observed variation worth checking.

Worked example

Provided rises: 7 1/2, 7 9/16, 7 1/2, 7 7/16, 7 1/2 in.
Highest - lowest = 7 9/16 - 7 7/16 = 1/8 in.
Observed spread is 1/8 in. A compliance decision would also require the applicable stair requirements and measurement confidence.

Individual exit key

Spread 1/8 in. Repeat selected risers with consistent endpoints and an independent checked reference; explain the expected result if setup caused the variation.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 1.4 · Reversal and instrument checks
bodyHtml:
1.4 · Reversal and instrument checks

Target: tr.u2.level-check; drawing: tr.u2.plumb-level

Materials

Horizontal spirit level, stable surface, removable marks.

Fallback

Analyze the supplied paired readings and state that tool handling was not observed.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. Repeat and investigate; direction alone is insufficient.

Worked example

Supplied room-referenced readings: first +2 divisions, reversed 0 divisions.
The readings differ by 2 divisions. In an ideal symmetric check, half-difference corresponds to a 1-division instrument offset.
Do not convert divisions to angle or length without the vial sensitivity; repeat the check and verify contact.

Individual exit key

They could share a bias or disagree for several reasons. Use marked-location reversal and model-specific instructions with repeated readings; a field check supports suitability within stated limits, not perfect accuracy.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Target: tr.u2.rise-run; drawing: tr.u2.plan-slope

Worked example

0.25/12 = 1/48; (1/48) x 100 = 2.0833%.

Fallback

Analyze supplied trial data: at slopes 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 in/ft, distances 12/13/11, 18/19/18, 22/24/23 in. These are simulated examples.

B. Change slope while keeping other planned conditions consistent and repeat trials.

Opening key

B. Pipe OD plus fall plus both specified clearances.

Worked example

Dry bay: run 16 ft; slope 1/4 in/ft; OD 2 3/8 in; top and bottom clearances 1 in each.
Fall = 4 in. Required depth = 1 + 2 3/8 + 4 + 1 = 8 3/8 in.
A 7 1/2-inch available depth is short by 7/8 inch.

Individual exit key

Available fall = 7.5 - 2.375 - 2 = 3.125 in. Maximum run = 3.125/0.25 = 12.5 ft. This is not authorization to alter framing.

Target: tr.u2.bay-conflict; drawing: tr.u2.plan-slope

Materials

Opening key

B. A calculation showing the violated constraint and the amount.

Worked example

Practice calculation: run 10 ft, slope 1/4 in/ft, OD 2 3/8 in, top and bottom clearances 3/4 in.
Fall 2 1/2 in; required depth 3/4 + 2 3/8 + 2 1/2 + 3/4.
Required depth 6 5/8 in. Use the different values on Case B for the assessed task.

Individual exit key

Use Case B key: 18-foot original needs 8 3/8 inches and exceeds 8 by 3/8. Shorter 16-foot route needs 7 7/8; deeper 8 1/2-inch zone fits original with 1/8 margin. Neither margin includes unspecified fittings.
